newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN IN PROPERTY SALE WORTH 3 BLN FFR GROSS.
newsitem.headline: GAN IN PROPERTY SALE WORTH 3 BLN FFR GROSS.

text.p: French insurer GAN said on Friday in a statement it had reached a protocol agreement with Morgan Stanley and Constructa to sell property assets with a gross value of three billion francs ($476.6 million).
The property belonged to its two defeasance vehicles Baticredit and Parixel.
It said the purchase price was higher than estimates used on December 31, 1996 to determine the cost of the state's commitment to GAN as part of its support of the defeasance vehicles.
Constructa is a property development company headquartered in Paris and Miami. It has extensive operations in Europe and in the United States.
GAN said in May that its aim was to sell 3.8 billion francs of net assets with a nominal value of 16.9 billion francs in the coming months.

A spokeswoman for GAN, which is due to be privatised, would not reveal the sale price. But market sources earlier said that they believed the assets being auctioned were worth up to one billion francs.
Some 75 real estate properties, bought when property prices were at their peak, are covered by the transaction.

The auction was handled by Bankers Trust. Others companies which reportedly had also been interested included Whitehall Street Real Estate LP, a fund managed by Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers and Wilshire Financial Services Group.
Property investment professionals were particuarly interested in the disposal as it was the first large sale of physical assets rather than loans.
Commercial properties made up 54 percent of the real estate sold, offices composed 38 percent, while the rest was housing.
More than 60 percent of the property was in the Paris region.
